coverage: Curated, non-exhaustive election-administration and legal incidents reviewed through October 22, 2026. Court actions and local administrative issues are separate mechanisms; newspaper leads without source confirmation are not verified incidents. Incident rows are not unique disenfranchised voters. Nine geographically indexed DHS injunction entries are ONE case; federal mail rule recorded at MA filing venue is NOT a Massachusetts-only voter-impact incident.

methodology.primary_metric: Potentially affected voters or ballots, only when grounded in a cited primary source
count_rules: Never equate records flagged, lawsuits filed, or challenges submitted with votes lost.
Record separate counts for potentially exposed, confirmed affected, remedied, and unresolved; unknown values are null.
Never subtract remediations from exposure without proof they refer to the same population.
Never sum potentially overlapping incidents into a statewide unique-voter total.
Preserve units: voters, ballots, registrations, and records are not interchangeable.
Store earliest/latest date, geographic scope, mechanism, source and verification status for each incident.
Do not infer partisan effects or probability of fraud from incident counts.

monitoring_priority_v1.definition: 0–100 provisional operational monitoring score, NOT a probability of fraud or a calibrated probability of affected voters.
scoring_rules: Documented voter-list disclosure litigation without shown voting-access consequences: 4 points.
Documented change to early-voting opportunity: 18 points; +2 when the change covers at least 10 counties.
Documented voter-registration transmission/processing incident: 25 points; -4 if the transfer defect is officially reported fixed but processing outcomes remain unverified.
Never use raw registration-record counts as counts of unique voters at risk.
Unverified reports cannot increase the index. Fully resolved cases require manual review rather than automatic treatment as active.
A state's provisional score is the maximum distinct documented incident score, not the sum of litigation, press articles or overlapping incidents.
Actual confirmed disenfranchisement would trigger a re-review and replacement of this starter rubric, not an arbitrary automatic extra point.
monitoring_priority_v1.missingness: Absence of an incident in the curated tracker is Not assessed, not 0. Unknown probabilities and voter counts remain null.
monitoring_priority_v1.roadmap: Move to severity × bounded unique voter exposure × probability of the precisely defined adverse outcome, once incident-level estimates are supported and can be reviewed.

probability_model_v0.headline: Subjective scenario probability, not a measured statistical frequency or fraud probability.
probability_model_v0.common_event: At least 100 distinct otherwise-eligible voters cannot cast a countable ballot solely because of the specified incident, by the conclusion of ordinary ballot review.
probability_model_v0.method: Transparent judgmental starting priors by observed mechanism, discounted for documented remedies and alternative voting opportunities. Rounded point assessments with wide explicit ranges. No observed frequencies or empirical calibration claimed.
priors: Direct registration processing backlog with remediation opportunities: 12% central, 3–30% subjective range.
Reduction in voting-time options with alternative voting opportunities: 10% central, 2–25% subjective range.
Litigation with no implemented voting-access change: 1% central, 0.1–5% subjective range.
caveats: The ranges are analysts' working assumptions, not probability distributions calibrated from historical outcomes.
Numbers refer to an adverse operational access outcome affecting at least 100 people, not to fraud, vote suppression intent, or an altered election result.
A documented decrease in voting convenience may be certain even if 100 people failing to vote is unlikely.
No automatic partisan adjustments; source conditions, remedies and actual ballot outcomes drive updates.
An incident's reported records, counties or historical Sunday turnout may contextualize exposure but are not counts of disenfranchised voters.

incidents.title: Maine — DOJ voter-list disclosure litigation
incidents.mechanism: Voter-list disclosure litigation
incidents.summary: Dismissed at district court; appeal ongoing. Litigation concerns access to statewide voter-list data; no count of eligible voters denied voting is established by this source.

sources.publisher: National Conference of State Legislatures

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible voters become unable to cast countable ballots by the conclusion of normal review as a direct consequence of voter-list changes resulting from this litigation. Filing or pursuing a lawsuit alone does not satisfy the scenario.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: Not established; requires voter-level deduplication, affected voters and counterfactual access data.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: 1% subjective reference scenario probability (0.1–5% uncertainty range). These voter-list disclosure lawsuits have no documented ballot-access change. A new operational order, implemented voter removal, or proof of adverse access impact would require immediate reassessment. Not calibrated from historical cases.

exposure_proxy.notes: Statewide voter list access is not itself a population of disenfranchised voters.

incidents.title: Texas registration-record transmission backlog
incidents.mechanism: Registration processing
incidents.summary: Texas Secretary of State spokesperson said on October 14 that county officials had cleared the previously delayed DPS voter-registration/update backlog of more than 500,000 records; no counties were known to still be processing that backlog. This confirms reported ADMINISTRATIVE CLEARANCE of the original backlog, not that every registration record was a distinct voter or that no individual was affected. A separate October 16 texas.gov address-validation error (about 15,000 records) is tracked separately.
incidents.count_source_notes: Reported statewide backlog of at least 500,000 registration and update records; does not establish unique individuals or ballots.

sources.publisher: Texas Secretary of State Elections Division (Sept. 22 directive)
Texas Tribune / Votebeat
Texas Secretary of State — county processing help, Sept. 25
Votebeat / Texas Tribune — provisional ballot remedy, Sept. 22
Texas Tribune — system glitches slowing processing, Oct. 5
Texas Secretary of State spokesperson quoted by Votebeat / Texas Tribune, Oct 14, 2026

incidents.process_status: Original DPS transfer backlog reportedly fully cleared by Texas counties as of Oct 14; separate October address-validation issue tracked separately; ballot-level impact still unknown.
incidents.scope_note: Records, not unique voters or lost votes

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 distinct otherwise-eligible Texans fail to cast countable ballots by conclusion of ordinary review because their timely DPS-related registrations or updates remained unprocessed despite available remedies.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: Not established; requires voter-level deduplication, affected voters and counterfactual access data.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: Earlier subjective 12% probability from October 13 withdrawn from current display after confirmed backlog clearance. Remaining individual voter effects are not quantified.

exposure_proxy.notes: Documented backlog volume, NOT unique voters, not the upper bound on all delayed transactions, and not ballots lost.

incidents.title: Sunday early-voting hours removed in 10 counties
incidents.mechanism: Early voting schedule
incidents.summary: The state elections board approved early-voting plans eliminating Sunday hours in ten counties that offered them in 2022. This is a change in access options; the number of voters whose ballots are affected is unknown.

sources.publisher: NC Newsline
NC State Board of Elections

incidents.process_status: Early-voting schedule approved; Sunday hours removed in 10 counties relative to 2022
incidents.scope_note: No count of voters unable to cast a ballot established

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible North Carolina voters who would use the discontinued Sunday early-voting hours in the named 10 counties do not cast a countable ballot by the conclusion of ordinary review, despite other voting opportunities.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: Not established; requires voter-level deduplication, affected voters and counterfactual access data.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: 10% subjective central estimate (2–25% range) for >=100 otherwise-eligible voters unable to cast countable ballots as a direct consequence of the removed Sunday hours. Downward factor: other early-voting days, election-day and mail options remain. Upward uncertainty: access constraints for Sunday-dependent voters; historical county Sunday turnout and alternate-hours capacity are not yet quantified. No calibrated turnout counterfactual.

exposure_proxy.notes: Geographic scope, NOT number of people prevented from voting. 2022 county Sunday voting figures still require retrieval.

incidents.title: North Carolina — 1,392 planned SAVE citizenship-check letters
incidents.mechanism: Official election-administration notice to voters flagged for additional citizenship verification
incidents.summary: On October 13 the State Board of Elections announced plans to send letters during the week to 1,392 registered voters flagged by federal SAVE data, after additional agency reviews. The board explicitly says a letter does not cancel registration or automatically bar voting, and no one is removed solely on SAVE information. Source does not establish that the mailings have been delivered, anyone is ineligible, or any eligible voter has lost a countable ballot.

sources.publisher: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Oct. 13, 2026 press release

incidents.scope_label: 1,392 registrants slated for SAVE follow-up letters
incidents.scope_note: Number of registered voter records selected for planned correspondence, from the Board's Oct. 13 announcement, not confirmed mailed letters or unique eligible voters denied voting.
incidents.process_status: Board announced notification and review; no automatic removal from notice alone

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible NC registrants become unable to cast countable November 2026 ballots solely because of this citizenship-notice process after ordinary review and remedies; receiving a letter alone does not meet the definition.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: Not quantified: requires verified removal/challenge outcomes, eligible-person identity, correction and provisional ballot disposition.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: Insufficient evidence to estimate a probability of countable ballots lost; the official source explicitly rules out automatic removal or cancellation based solely on the notice.

exposure_proxy.unit: registered voters selected for planned letters
exposure_proxy.qualifier: announced notification scope, NOT ballots lost
exposure_proxy.notes: Official Oct. 13 statement after additional state checks; no verified removal or ballot-prevention count. Do not conflate recipients with affected eligible voters.

incidents.title: California — federal 48-hour citizenship-review demand
incidents.mechanism: Federal demand for state/local voting-record eligibility review shortly before the general election
incidents.summary: The October 13 DOJ demand for 48-hour state citizenship review was followed by an October 15 federal lawsuit seeking to set aside vote-by-mail ballots from a federal list of approximately 20,000 purported likely noncitizens until citizenship verification. The lawsuit, DOJ's allegation and California's opposition are DOCUMENTED; the accuracy of the 20,000-person identification and any consequential wrongful ballot rejections are unverified. DOJ acknowledged the list may include citizens. California contests the reliability and timing. No court-authorized segregation of these ballots has been verified as of October 22.

sources.publisher: California Secretary of State, press release PR26-127, October 14, 2026
U.S. Department of Justice complaint announcement, Oct 15, 2026
California Attorney General opposition filing, Oct 20, 2026

incidents.scope_label: ~20,000 flagged names alleged by DOJ; eligible voters and ballot impacts unverified
incidents.scope_note: The federal government's asserted list size is not a count of noncitizens, eligible voters denied ballots, or voters whose ballots were actually set aside.
incidents.process_status: Federal complaint filed Oct 15; motion to sequester questioned ballots pending judicial determination. Defendant state contests; no verified ballot outcomes.

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible California residents ultimately cannot cast countable 2026 federal ballots solely due to this 48-hour eligibility demand or a resulting enforced action after ordinary correction and remedies.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: No independently verified eligible-voter population, removal records, ballot challenges or disposition outcomes.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: No credible quantified exposure-to-ballot-loss linkage or implemented voter-list change established by the reviewed official statement.

exposure_proxy.notes: The 48-hour deadline is not an exposure count. Reported suspected-noncitizen figures have not been verified as unique ineligible people, and cannot proxy lost eligible ballots.

incidents.title: California — federal court order restricting DHS voter-investigation field operations
incidents.mechanism: Unlawful Voter Initiative field-interview policy and election-related investigative operations
incidents.shared_case_note: ONE federal order covering nine states, represented once per jurisdiction for geographic discovery. Do not count as nine independent federal actions or sum overlapping case impacts.
incidents.summary: On October 21, 2026, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin issued a preliminary injunction restricting specified DHS election-related field operations and interviews involving people known or reasonably suspected to be U.S. citizens, and operations based solely on the cited TECS matching records, in nine named states. The court discussed unreliable source lists and chilling effects on voter-assistance activity. IMPORTANT: the injunction itself was stayed until 5 p.m. California time Friday, October 23 to permit appeal; it must not be shown as already in force on October 22. The order is not a finding that any specified number of eligible ballots was uncounted.
incidents.process_status: Preliminary injunction ordered October 21 but stayed by its own terms until October 23 at 5 p.m. PT; appeal/bond status after that deadline not yet verified.
incidents.scope_label: 9-state judicial order; state-level eligible voter impacts unknown
incidents.scope_note: The same court order appears in nine state views; no numerical count of disenfranchised voters is established.

sources.publisher: United States District Court for the Northern District of California, Document 87, October 21, 2026

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 distinct otherwise-eligible voters in this state ultimately fail to cast countable ballots because of the specified federal field-interview activities, despite normal correction and voting remedies.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: No unique-voter denominator, state-specific exposure totals, or established ballot-loss observations in the order.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: Not estimated: court-identified intimidation of voter assistance cannot be responsibly mapped onto 100 lost countable ballots from this source.

exposure_proxy.notes: Court document discusses source record counts and investigatory activities, not distinct eligible voters whose ballots went uncounted.

incidents.title: Wisconsin — federal court order restricting DHS voter-investigation field operations
incidents.mechanism: Unlawful Voter Initiative field-interview policy and election-related investigative operations
incidents.shared_case_note: ONE federal order covering nine states, represented once per jurisdiction for geographic discovery. Do not count as nine independent federal actions or sum overlapping case impacts.
incidents.summary: On October 21, 2026, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin issued a preliminary injunction restricting specified DHS election-related field operations and interviews involving people known or reasonably suspected to be U.S. citizens, and operations based solely on the cited TECS matching records, in nine named states. The court discussed unreliable source lists and chilling effects on voter-assistance activity. IMPORTANT: the injunction itself was stayed until 5 p.m. California time Friday, October 23 to permit appeal; it must not be shown as already in force on October 22. The order is not a finding that any specified number of eligible ballots was uncounted.
incidents.process_status: Preliminary injunction ordered October 21 but stayed by its own terms until October 23 at 5 p.m. PT; appeal/bond status after that deadline not yet verified.

incidents.title: Texas — separate October address-update validation glitch
incidents.mechanism: State texas.gov address-validation software error delaying registration name/address changes
incidents.summary: A separate address-validation problem affected updates made since September 1. A Texas Secretary of State spokesperson reported approximately 15,000 records were retransmitted to counties by October 16 and the software issue corrected. County-by-county completion of the resulting updates and individual ballot consequences remain unverified. This is distinct from the earlier 500,000+ DPS backlog; counts are not added as unique voters.
incidents.count_source_notes: Texas Secretary of State spokesperson reported sending approximately 15,000 affected records to counties. These are registration/update records, not 15,000 proven unique voters or ballots.
incidents.scope_note: Record count, NOT measured disenfranchisement. Includes corrections and updates; overlap with earlier backlog and unique-voter coverage cannot be assumed.
incidents.process_status: State reports technical defect corrected and records sent by October 16; final county processing and ballot outcomes unverified.

sources.publisher: Texas Secretary of State spokesperson, quoted by The Texas Newsroom / KUT October 16, 2026

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible Texans fail to cast countable ballots as a direct result of the separate address-update validation failure after ordinary correction and provisional-ballot review.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: No deduplicated voter universe or failure-to-vote data; registered addresses are not ballots.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: No measured link from these retransmitted records to lost countable ballots.

exposure_proxy.notes: Retransmitted records, not distinct voters, not confirmed pending registrations or lost votes.

incidents.title: Bexar County — Leon Valley early-voting ballot scanner jams
incidents.mechanism: Voting equipment malfunction and temporary waiting-time disruption
incidents.summary: Bexar County Elections Administrator Michele Carew confirmed to KSAT that ballot scanners jammed at the Leon Valley Conference Center during early voting. Voters described waits of up to approximately two hours. Carew said technicians would be placed at locations and emergency ballot bins could be used; ballots deposited in emergency bins would be counted at headquarters. This is a confirmed operational disruption, NOT proof that accepted ballots were lost or that the outcome was altered.
incidents.scope_label: One documented Leon Valley polling site; ballot loss unknown
incidents.scope_note: The reported two-hour waits are an upper observed wait, not the number or share of voters who failed to vote. One reporter said at least one voter planned to return later.
incidents.process_status: Scanner issue acknowledged by county official; emergency-bin remedy described. Follow-up repair status and eligible-voter outcomes not independently verified.

sources.publisher: KSAT interview with Bexar County Elections Administrator Michele Carew, October 20, 2026

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 eligible Bexar voters ultimately fail to cast countable 2026 general-election ballots specifically because of scanner jams at the Leon Valley early-voting location, despite emergency-bin and repeat-visit options.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: No independently established distinct eligible-voter count or recorded uncounted-ballot outcome.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: No empirical count of eligible voters ultimately unable to cast countable ballots; administrative disruption does not establish voter disenfranchisement.

exposure_proxy.notes: Wait durations and scanner capacity are not observed counts of eligible voters prevented from voting.

incidents.title: Bexar County — missing local measures on some early-voting ballots
incidents.mechanism: Ballot configuration error affecting local propositions
incidents.summary: Bexar County Elections Administrator Michele Carew confirmed to KSAT that some early-voting ballots omitted local measures including Northside and East Central school-district propositions, and that the issue was corrected within approximately one hour after discovery. She said voters should alert a judge before casting if any race or measure is missing and that cast ballots could not be changed. Number of voters who cast an incomplete ballot and eventual local-contest impacts are unverified. Do not conflate this local-proposition issue with statewide Senate vote integrity.
incidents.scope_label: Some early ballots omitted local measures; number cast unknown
incidents.scope_note: The estimated one-hour correction window is not a count of affected ballots, denied votes, voters, or election-changing errors.
incidents.process_status: County official reports ballot-programming issue corrected; audit of already-cast ballots and scope of local propositions remains unverified.

incidents.title: Bexar County — delayed voter registration card printing and mailing
incidents.mechanism: Voter-registration card printing and mailing backlog
incidents.summary: Bexar County Elections Administrator Michele Carew told KSAT the county had a registration-card printing bottleneck and about 45,000 cards ready to mail. A spring mass mailing reportedly involved more than 130,000 registered voters, but those quantities must not be treated as lost ballots or unique voters prevented from voting. Election officials said registration cards are not required when a voter has accepted alternative identification.
incidents.scope_label: ~45,000 cards awaiting mailing; registration not invalidated
incidents.scope_note: Reported 45,000 card backlog and earlier 130,000-person mailing refer to different administrative scopes; do not combine or use as confirmed disenfranchisement.
incidents.process_status: Printing/mailout backlog officially described; individual mailing delivery and any effect on ballot access remain unverified.

sources.publisher: KSAT interview with Bexar County Elections Administrator Michele Carew, October 20, 2026

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible voters fail to cast countable ballots solely because of delayed registration-card mailings after use of available voter-ID alternatives.

incidents.title: Federal USPS mail-ballot portal and envelope rules enjoined before November election
incidents.mechanism: Federal ballot-mail rule challenged in district court; protective preliminary injunction
incidents.summary: On September 4, the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts preliminarily blocked listed requirements of a new USPS federal ballot-mail rule for elections on or before November 3, including envelope approval requirements and mandatory portal enrollment. Massachusetts Attorney General confirmed the injunction as part of a multistate challenge. This court finding concerns a federal rule, NOT a Massachusetts-specific voting problem. Some executive-order provisions remain separately disputed; verify later appellate orders before treating the injunction as final.
incidents.scope_label: Federal USPS rule preliminarily enjoined; no ballot loss established
incidents.scope_note: The case venue is Massachusetts but the affected rule concerned federal mail voting; this record must not be tallied as Massachusetts-specific affected voters.
incidents.process_status: Preliminary injunction documented September 4 for elections through November 3; appellate posture after October 22 not independently verified.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Attorney General, September 4, 2026
United States District Court for the District of Massachusetts, September 4 preliminary-injunction order

incidents.shared_case_note: One federal rule case, filed in Massachusetts; not evidence of Massachusetts-only affected votes.

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 distinct eligible voters ultimately lose a countable federal ballot solely because of enforcement of the challenged mandatory USPS envelope or portal provisions despite the September preliminary injunction.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: No independently established distinct eligible-voter count or recorded uncounted-ballot outcome.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: No empirical count of eligible voters ultimately unable to cast countable ballots; administrative disruption does not establish voter disenfranchisement.
